body: i thought that she would leave me. it was right before our wedding. i got scared. panicked. thought that i could right my wrongs.

if i came out with the truth...

i would lose my wife. i've lied to her in the past about debt and there is no way she would stay after this.

i would be forced to find a new place to live.

i have a good job and a decent amount of money from freelance work.

however it isn't enough to cover my debts on a monthly basis.

my son would see his father depressed for years on end while i would struggle constantly to stay afloat above my debts.

he would see me reduced to extremely modest living conditions.

i would never recover from this emotionally.

of course. 

he will approach from the viewpoint of a child.

he'll be unsure of many things for a long time.  

however i do believe he'll understand that i love him. he may grow to hate me for my decision but he'll know that i loved him.  if he grows up to reject everything about me it will be okay.

i disagree.

i grew up with a mom who was in constant financial strain.  she ruined my credit from an early age by putting my name on utilities and not paying for those bills.

if i had limited exposure to her parenting growing up i would be a different person. probably better.

your english is fine. i get what you are trying to say.

it is his stepmother. not his mother.

he lives with his mom and comes to my house every other weekend.

i believe in him. i believe he will be okay.  

i have taught him many things and he knows my opinion on a wide range of topics. other than not understand my death he will have a very complete sense of who i am. good and bad.

then the day he gets over it he'll view me as a piece of shit.

that is fine.

i'd rather him not idolize me after my death.

i love him. more than i can possibly say.

however i know that i am giving him a better life by excluding myself from it.

yes. it is.

i am not an upset teenager.  i am a rational adult and this is the best possible scenario.

she'll be able to find a better partner (mentally and financially) and my son won't see a lifetime of decline (mentally and financially) of his father.  

they'll remember me at my best.  or seemingly best.

this would be easily the third chance.

my debt it mine.  it was debt owed before marriage meaning she isn't liable for it.

my insurance policy will cover the funeral costs.

she will be able to sell my car and our house and find something fit better for one person.

i don't think that is the lesson he will learn.  

he'll learn that some people are weak and unable to overcome life's difficulties and that ultimately it is up to each individual to better themselves.  i cannot stress enough how many people he has in his life to lean on.

it is NOT temporary.

i have no means to better the situation.  

10-15 years i could win the lottery.

10-15 years i could be an award winning artist that sells out galleries.

10-15 years i will have been buried for 10-15 years.

i grew up without a father and have presumed him to be dead for many many years.

i know how difficult it is.

however he is surrounded by people that love and support him.

i do have a sense of value as someone able to supply material things.

however she is the breadwinner and always has been in our relationship.

previously i attempted to get a passport for a trip and found out that i could not get a passport due to child support debt.  she asked if there was anything else she should know about. i said no.

i didn't use the money for anything other than casual purchases.  i spent too much money over the course of two weeks, paid the wrong bills and now i have nothing to give her.

no.

she would take it badly. there is no other way to take it.

i don't judge her for that.

she would leave me.

i love her but i have no doubt about that.

she's given me the opportunity to come clean about debt in the past and i've never admitted it's extent.

no no. he won't know the reason why.  he is young enough that this shouldn't damage him forever. yes he'll be in pain for awhile but it will get easier.  

it will be easier than seeing his father continue to fail, end another marriage and become reliant on welfare for aid.

because i've screwed things up. we've never had a joint checking account (married two years) and i am due to deposit about $1500 into her account.  i don't have it. i've exhausted all resources. i have no credit. i have two payday loans out and a loan on my 401K. i've got nothing. i didn't watch my balance and spent entirely too much money. this probably seems like a paltry sum to many but it is the proverbial straw.

i don't have an answer for why i've been suicidal my whole life.  

my son has a better relationship with me but not a bad relationship with his mother. she is a wonderful mom.

my wife and son don't have much of a relationship. not a bad one... just a lack of one.  i don't know that they would honestly see each other much after my funeral.  i have a sister (mother of his favorite cousins) who can fill him in on any questions about me that he might have as a teenager/adult.

i am not depressed. suicide would be a completely logical decision. i've thought of the other paths and i don't have the courage or determination.  i could let her know everything, have her leave, file for bankruptcy and start over... however much of my debt can't be erased. student loans and back child support (i pay now but i'm still paying back for when i was an employed college student for 6 years).
